newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's import growth rate 4.8 pct last year.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's import growth rate 4.8 pct last year.

text.p: Indonesia's import growth rate declined to 4.8 percent in 1996 compared with 30.5 percent in the previous year, the official Antara news agency reported on Saturday.

Antara quoted Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo as saying on Friday that more export-oriented industries had been using locally-produced materials which reduced the country's dependence on imports.
"We are glad that the increasing domestic production has pushed down the import growth rate," Ariwibowo was quoted as saying after meeting President Suharto.

Ariwibowo said the value of Indonesian exports totalled $40.6 billion in January-October 1996, of which $31.2 billion was derived from non-oil and gas exports and $9.3 billion from oil and natural gas.
Imports in the period cost $35.3 billion, of which $31.2 billion was non-oil and gas and $2.7 billion oil and gas,
"Considering the figures, we concluded there is a surplus of $5.2 billion.," he said.
